The only direct callers of `OrderSetService.saveOrderSet` in the REST module are in the `openmrs1_12` order set resource and order set member resource, plus one test. Each of them would see any change in that method's behaviour.

Falkon has the repo as `github.com/openmrs/openmrs-module-webservices.rest`, so I used that name. I did not check `openmrs-core` itself or the module's other versioned resources.

1. **`OrderSetResource1_12.save`** (lines 58–72) is the main caller. It resolves member concepts and order types by UUID, then returns `Context.getOrderSetService().saveOrderSet(orderSet)`. This is the path for creating and updating order sets over REST.
2. **`OrderSetMemberResource1_12.save`** (lines 163–168) adds a member to its parent order set and calls `saveOrderSet(parent)`, so member creation over REST depends on it.
3. **`OrderSetMemberResource1_12.purge`** (lines 171–175) removes a member from its order set and calls `saveOrderSet(orderSet)`.
4. **`OrderSetMemberResource1_12.delete`** (lines 151–155) retires a member and calls `saveOrderSet(orderSet)`. This is a protected override of the base class's delete.
5. **`OrderSetMemberController1_12Test.shouldShowAllOrderSetMembersForAnOrderSet`** (lines 80–100) calls `saveOrderSet` directly in test setup. The end line is an estimate, because I only read up to line 94.
